description: Change semantics for every module field cluster:vm owns — the reference manifest for ADR-020 D3/D4.
_note: Every class below is a STATEMENT OF EXISTING BEHAVIOUR, read off update-service.sh as it stood before ADR-020: what it applies via the single batched `qm set`, what it grows, what it migrates, what it warns about and what it refuses. Nothing here changes what happens today; P3 makes update-service.sh read this file instead of hardcoding the same knowledge in an imperative drift loop.

vmname.note: Proxmox spells the guest name 'name'. Only reconciled when the guest reports one.

vmtag.note: Proxmox stores tags lowercased, de-duplicated and ';'-joined; module JSON may use mixed case and commas. The 'tags' normalizer is that canonicalisation, moved from update-service.sh's normalize_tags into the one differ. defaultIsDesired:false is that script's `__none__` sentinel, declared: a module that does not set vmtag has its live tags LEFT ALONE, not overwritten with the schema's 'TAPPaaS'.

cputype.note: Proxmox spells it 'cpu'. The undeclared default resolves to 'host' — from module-fields.json, via the one resolver, NOT from a cfg() ladder in this service (#550).

bridge0.note: A bridge change moves the guest to a different L2 segment, so it must re-DHCP — hence the reboot.

zone0.note: The zone resolves to net0's VLAN tag; a new tag is a new subnet, so the guest must renew DHCP and re-register DNS.

mac0.note: Applies live on the bridge — no reboot. When the module pins no mac0 the LIVE MAC is preserved, which is why the manager (not the hook) assembles the finished netopts string.

trunks0.note: A trunk-only change applies live on the bridge — no reboot.

bridge1.note: Also the ADD/REMOVE switch for the second NIC. Its module-fields.json default is the sentinel 'NONE', so an undeclared bridge1 resolves to 'no second NIC' — the same reading Create-TAPPaaS-VM.sh and update-service.sh have always had. 'NONE' with a live net1 means the NIC is removed, which likewise reboots.

diskSize.note: Grow goes through resize-disk.sh. A SHRINK is refused at apply time (hook exit 20), not by the static pre-gate: whether a change is a grow or a shrink is only knowable against the live size. defaultIsDesired:false because an undeclared diskSize means 'leave the disk alone' — resizing every undeclared guest to the schema's install-time 8G would be a shrink on almost all of them.

node.note: The ADR-019 bridge. The hook routes HA-vs-non-HA internally: a module that dependsOn cluster:ha has its node drift handled by the HA rule (re-point), a plain module by qm migrate. Live-OK decides whether the migrate needs downtime, so this refuses (exit 10) rather than migrating offline without --force.

storage.note: A storage change means moving the disk. update-service.sh has always warned rather than acting, because an implicit qm move-disk is a long, IO-heavy operation an operator must schedule. NOT pre-gated: writing the intended storage into config and reporting the gap is useful, so only the apply refuses. defaultIsDesired:false — an undeclared storage is not a claim that the disk belongs on the schema's 'tanka1'.

bios.note: Firmware is chosen when the guest is created; changing it on a live VM is refused today (the script's only FATAL). Pre-gated, so config is never left claiming a firmware the guest does not have. defaultIsDesired:false — an undeclared bios is not compared against the live firmware at all, which is what keeps a guest installed on seabios from reporting permanent drift against the schema's 'ovmf'.

ostype.note: A creation-time hint that selects emulated hardware defaults; never reconciled on a live guest.

autoInstall.note: Drives the unattended install at creation. Meaningless afterwards.

sshAccess.note: Seeds the cloud-init SSH configuration at creation.

vmid.note: The guest's identity. Changing it IS a different guest — delete + reinstall.

os.note: The installed operating system. Auto-detected from the image at install; changing it means reinstalling.

imageType.note: clone vs. download decides how the guest was built; it cannot be re-decided in place.

cloudInit.note: Whether the guest was provisioned via cloud-init — a property of how it was created.

net0.note: The primary NIC: one qm value 'virtio=<mac>,bridge=<b>,tag=<vlan>[,trunks=…][,queues=…]' assembled from four declared fields. The MANAGER builds the finished string because it must preserve two LIVE values the config never carries — the MAC when the module pins none, and queues, which must never change on a running NIC (#194). in-place-reboot is the CEILING: the runner escalates only when bridge0 or zone0 actually drifted; a MAC- or trunk-only change stays in-place, exactly as today.

net1.note: The optional second NIC. Adding it, or changing its bridge/tag, reboots; a trunk- or MAC-only change applies live. Removing it (bridge1 gone from config while the guest still has net1) is a `qm set --delete net1` and also reboots.
